the v2 adapters read from store_v2/query.py (index-v2.db), NOT m6_*

production_write_authority.evidence_summary: The v2 store (store_v2/publish.py + store_v2/worlds.py writing index-v2.db) is the production WRITE authority. v2_write_authority defaults to True (M4-7, settings.py:517), so the v2 World context is always built (runner.py:744) and v2 World finalization is the AUTHORITATIVE success criterion for an indexing run (runner.py:945, 971). The legacy index.db is opened ONLY in explicit compat mode (_legacy_compat_on() defaults False, runner.py:501-524).

m6_status.evidence_summary: M6 is SHADOW-ONLY. The m6_store, m6_schema, and m6_indexing modules are explicitly marked SHADOW-ONLY in their docstrings, are NEVER imported by the production read path (query.py, v2_shadow_adapters.py) or the production write path (runner.py, publish.py, worlds.py), and their only consumer is the research/shadow-differential-test function index_corpus_into_m6_store. Production query paths still hit the v2 store until shadow differential testing (§34) proves QUERY_PARITY_FAILURES == 0.

v2_status.verdict: AUTHORITATIVE (the current production read + write authority)
v2_status.evidence_summary: The v2 engine (the M3B/M4/M5 native engine backed by index-v2.db) is the current production authority for BOTH reads and writes. M3B (v2 read engine) is complete and default-on since M3. M4 (v2 write finalization authority) is complete with v2_write_authority=True default (M4-7). M5 (v2-only default) means normal operation writes/reads ONLY the v2 store; the legacy index.db is an explicit opt-in compat island (FW_CONTEXT_LEGACY_COMPATIBILITY_MODE=1).

v2-only is the DEFAULT normal mode (M5 complete)
